title: China's Oldest Wooden Halls Use Zero Nails — 1,000+ Years Standing | China Travel Expert
description:
China's oldest surviving wooden hall was built in the year 782 — and like the great timber temples and pagodas that followed, it uses no nails at all. The weight is carried by dougong: interlocking wooden brackets locked together with mortise-and-tenon joints.

That flexibility is why they last. One all-wood pagoda from 1056 has ridden out more than 40 earthquakes in nearly a thousand years without falling.

🧭 Expert Tip: The best cluster of ancient timber architecture is in Shanxi — base yourself around Datong and Wutai Shan.

中国最古老的木构大殿建于公元782年——不用一根钉子,全靠斗拱榫卯,屹立千年、扛过40多次地震。
